verdict: Berkshire's operating earnings fell 14% to $9.6B as California wildfire losses halved insurance underwriting − and a $6.4B paper loss on its stock portfolio cut headline profit to $4.6B, down from $12.7B a year ago.

otherDetail: Investment losses of $6,435M — mostly paper losses on Berkshire's stock portfolio — plus $126M of equity-method earnings, less $69M attributable to noncontrolling interests.
footerNote: Berkshire has no single gross-profit line: costs are split following the 10-Q's own structure.
follow100Note: Paper losses on the stock portfolio took $7.17 of every $100 of revenue, on top of $87.23 of costs that included the California wildfire claims — leaving just $5.13 kept as profit. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Operating earnings fell 14%
takeaways.text: The businesses themselves earned $9.6B after tax, down from $11.2B − insurance underwriting dropped to $1.3B from $2.6B after roughly $860M of after-tax losses from the Southern California wildfires, and a currency swing on foreign debt dragged 'Other' earnings from $1.1B to $41M.

takeaways.title: A paper loss on the stock pile
takeaways.text: Investment losses of $6.4B before tax were mostly unrealized: stocks Berkshire still holds fell $6.8B in value, partly offset by small gains on stocks sold during the quarter ($4.7B of sales). After tax, the investment loss was $5.0B.

takeaways.title: The cash pile hit another record
takeaways.text: Cash and Treasury Bills at the insurance and other businesses rose to $342.4B, up from $330.8B at year-end — Berkshire sold $4.7B of stocks against $3.2B of purchases, parked the money in Treasury Bills, and bought back none of its own shares.

oneTimers: Southern California wildfires: the insurance businesses took about $1.1B of pre-tax catastrophe losses ($860M after tax) — the quarter's only significant catastrophe event, versus none a year ago. GEICO itself improved (pre-tax underwriting profit of $2,173M, up from $1,928M); the wildfire losses pushed the primary and reinsurance groups into underwriting losses.

Currency swing on foreign debt: revaluing Berkshire's euro-, pound- and yen-denominated borrowings produced a $936M pre-tax loss this quarter versus a $781M gain a year ago. The pre-tax loss sits inside selling, general and administrative expenses; after tax ($713M loss versus a $597M gain) it is the main reason 'Other' operating earnings fell from $1,078M to $41M.

Investment losses are mostly paper losses. Of the $5,038M after-tax investment losses, about $7.4B was a fall in unrealized gains on stocks Berkshire still holds, partly offset by $2.4B of after-tax realized gains on stocks sold. Next quarter the unrealized part can just as easily reverse.
